fw-strlen.prompt: Write `size_t c_strlen(const char *s)` without any library call.
ideas: Walk a second pointer to the NUL and return `p - s`.
The empty string needs no special case: the loop body never runs.
fw-strlen.bug: Counting in a narrow type like `uint8_t` or `int`, which overflows on long strings.

fw-reverse-cstr.prompt: Reverse a NUL-terminated string in place: `void reverse_cstr(char *s)`.
ideas: Find the end first, then swap with two pointers moving inward.
Stop when `lo >= hi`; the middle character of an odd-length string stays put.
fw-reverse-cstr.bug: Starting `hi` at the NUL, or computing `len - 1` as a huge `size_t` on the empty string.

fw-ptr-debug.prompt: Classify six `void *` expressions, then write, read, store and load through `void *` and step one byte past `p`.
ideas: `void *` can't be dereferenced or advanced: cast to the real type first, `*(int *)p` or `(uint8_t *)p + 1`.
A pointer stored in memory is accessed through `void **`: `*(void **)storage = val`.
A cast is not an lvalue, so `(void **)p = x` doesn't compile.
fw-ptr-debug.bug: `p + 1` on a `void *`: a GNU extension that compiles, so it hides in real code.

fw-ptr-swap.prompt: Swap two objects of any type: `void swap_values(void *a, void *b, size_t size)`.
ideas: Cast both to `uint8_t *` and swap byte by byte through a one-byte temporary.
No temp buffer, VLA or malloc; works for structs, doubles and pointers.
fw-ptr-swap.bug: A fixed-width temporary such as `uint32_t`, or XOR-swap, which zeroes the object when `a == b`.

fw-bounded-strings.prompt: Implement BSD `strlcpy`: copy at most `dstsize - 1` bytes, always terminate, return `strlen(src)`.
ideas: The return value is the source length, so `ret >= dstsize` tells the caller it truncated.
Keep counting the source after you stop copying.
`dstsize == 0`: write nothing at all.
fw-bounded-strings.bug: Writing the NUL at `dst[dstsize]`, or touching `dst` when `dstsize == 0`.

ideas: Compare bytes as `unsigned char`, so 0x80 and above sort after ASCII.
strcmp: advance while `*a && *a == *b`, then return the difference.
strstr: an empty needle returns `hay`; otherwise try each start position.
fw-strcmp-strstr.bug: Comparing plain `char`, which is signed on most targets, so 0x80 sorts below 'a'.

fw-array-ops.prompt: Reverse an `int32_t` array in place, and rotate it left by any `k` with O(1) extra space.
ideas: Rotate left by k: reverse `[0, k)`, reverse `[k, n)`, then reverse the whole array.
Reduce `k %= n` first, after returning early for `n <= 1`.
fw-array-ops.bug: `k % n` with `n == 0` (division by zero), or `size_t hi = n - 1` when `n == 0`.

ideas: Parenthesize every parameter and the whole expansion.
Use `1u`: `1 << 31` overflows a signed `int`.
bit-macros.bug: An unparenthesized `n`, so `SET_BIT(r, i + 1)` expands to the wrong shift.

power-of-two.prompt: `is_power_of_two(x)` and `round_up_pow2(x)` for 32-bit `x`, without looping over the bits.
ideas: Power of two: `x && !(x & (x - 1))`; `x & (x - 1)` clears the lowest set bit.
Round up: `x--`, smear with `x |= x >> 1, 2, 4, 8, 16`, then return `x + 1`.
Return 1 for `x == 0` before the decrement.
power-of-two.bug: Forgetting the `x &&`, so 0 counts as a power of two, or skipping the decrement, so exact powers double.

fw-bswap.prompt: Byte-swap 16- and 32-bit values with shifts and masks only.
ideas: 16-bit: `x << 8` produces an `int`; cast the result back to `uint16_t`.
fw-bswap.bug: Masking with the wrong constant after the shift, or returning bits above 0xFFFF from the 16-bit version.

fw-endian-detect.prompt: Detect host byte order at runtime and implement `htonl` without library calls.
ideas: Store `uint32_t one = 1` and read its first byte through a `uint8_t *`: 1 means little-endian.
`htonl` byte-swaps on a little-endian host and is the identity on a big-endian one.
fw-endian-detect.bug: Swapping unconditionally, or deciding endianness with a compile-time macro.

fw-reg-bitfield.prompt: Set bits, clear bits, write a field and read a field of a 32-bit register value, given a mask and shift.
ideas: Write: `(reg & ~mask) | ((value << shift) & mask)`.
Read: `(reg & mask) >> shift`.
Mask the shifted value so an oversized value can't spill into neighbouring fields.
fw-reg-bitfield.bug: OR-ing in the new value without clearing the old field first.

fw-bit-suite.prompt: Popcount, bit reverse, and rotate left/right on `uint32_t`, with no builtins.
ideas: Popcount: `while (x) { x &= x - 1; n++; }` loops once per set bit.
Rotate: `n &= 31; if (n == 0) return x; return (x << n) | (x >> (32 - n));`
Reverse: shift bits out of `x` and into `r` 32 times, or swap halves, bytes, nibbles, pairs, then bits.
fw-bit-suite.bug: `x >> 32` when `n` is 0 or 32: undefined behavior that often returns `x | x`.

fw-int-promotion.prompt: Fix three sensor helpers (`sum_gt`, `all_ones`, `inv_hi_nibble`) that go wrong through implicit integer conversions.
ideas: Mixing `unsigned` and `int` converts the `int` to unsigned: -1 becomes UINT_MAX.
`~` and `>>` on a `uint8_t` act on the promoted `int`: cast back, `(uint8_t)~port >> 4`.
Write constants in the type you need: `~0u`, not `~0`.
fw-int-promotion.bug: Fixing with a cast to `int` or `long`, which still overflows when `int` is 16 bits.

fw-macro-pitfalls.prompt: Write `SECONDS_PER_YEAR`, `MIN(A, B)` and `WRITE_REG16(hi, lo, val)` macros that work in every context.
ideas: `(60UL * 60UL * 24UL * 365UL)`: the `UL` suffix keeps the product from overflowing a 16-bit `int`.
`((A) < (B) ? (A) : (B))`: parenthesize each parameter and the whole expansion.
Multi-statement macros go in `do { ... } while (0)`, and each argument is evaluated exactly once.
fw-macro-pitfalls.bug: A bare `{ ... }` body, which breaks `if (x) WRITE_REG16(...); else ...`.

fw-sizeof-var.prompt: `MY_SIZEOF_VAR(x)`: the size of a variable or array in bytes, without `sizeof`.
ideas: `((size_t)((char *)(&(x) + 1) - (char *)&(x)))`: one-past pointer minus start, in bytes.
`&arr + 1` steps over the whole array, so arrays give their full size.
fw-sizeof-var.bug: Subtracting the typed pointers, which gives 1, instead of casting to `char *` first.

ideas: offsetof: `((size_t)&((type *)0)->member)`.
container_of: `((type *)((char *)(ptr) - MY_OFFSETOF(type, member)))`.
Do the subtraction on a `char *`, so it counts bytes.
fw-offsetof.bug: Subtracting from `ptr` without the `char *` cast, which moves by `offset * sizeof(*ptr)`.

fw-func-ptr-decl.prompt: Write typedefs from `int` up to an array of function pointers, then a `dispatch` jump table.
ideas: Right-left rule: `int (*fp[10])(int)` is an array of 10 pointers to functions taking `int` and returning `int`.
`int (*p)[10]` is a pointer to an array; `int *a[10]` is an array of pointers.
`static int (*const ops[])(int, int) = {...};` and check `op < sizeof ops / sizeof ops[0]` before indexing.
fw-func-ptr-decl.bug: `op <= N` (off by one), or calling the divide before checking for zero.

fw-stack-growing-up.prompt: `bool is_stack_growing_up(void)`: detect the stack direction at runtime.
ideas: Pass the address of a local to a separate, non-inlined function and compare it with that function's own local.
Mark the helper `__attribute__((noinline))`.
fw-stack-growing-up.bug: Comparing two locals in the same function: the compiler can order a frame however it likes.

fw-bug-diagnosis.prompt: Fix `fix_bug1` (power-of-two check) and `fix_bug2` (clear bit i, toggle bit j), then name bugs 3–8.
ideas: `==` binds tighter than `&`: `n && (n & (n - 1)) == 0` needs parentheses around the AND.
Toggle is `^= (1u << j)`; the `~` belongs only to the clear.
3–8: volatile copied once, sizeof of a pointer, returned stack buffer, unbounded strcpy, `1 << 31`, unchecked index.
fw-bug-diagnosis.bug: Fixing the precedence but still reporting 0 as a power of two.

ideas: memmove: copy forward when `dst < src`, backward from the end otherwise.
Work through `unsigned char *`; memset writes `(unsigned char)value`; all three return `dst`.
fw-mem-primitives.bug: memmove copying forward when `dst` overlaps the tail of `src`, smearing the first bytes across the region.

fw-run-length-encode.prompt: Run-length encode a string as char + decimal count into a malloc'd result sized to the input.
ideas: Two passes: compute the exact output length (count the digits of each run), then allocate and write.
Run lengths can have several digits: write them with a digit loop, not `'0' + n`.
The empty string still returns a freeable `""`.
fw-run-length-encode.bug: Allocating without room for the terminator, or assuming every count is one digit.

fw-i32-to-dec.prompt: `bool i32_to_dec(char *out, size_t out_len, int32_t value)` without any printf.
ideas: Take the magnitude as unsigned: `u = value < 0 ? 0u - (uint32_t)value : (uint32_t)value`.
Emit digits least significant first into a temp buffer, then copy them out reversed.
Check that digits + sign + NUL fit before writing anything.

fw-parse-i32.prompt: `bool parse_i32(const char *s, int32_t *out)`: optional sign, digits only, false on overflow or junk.
ideas: Check before you multiply: reject when `acc > (limit - d) / 10`.
Use a limit of 2147483648 for a minus sign so INT32_MIN parses (accumulate in `uint32_t`, or in the negative range).
Reject the empty string, a lone sign, and any non-digit.
fw-parse-i32.bug: Checking for overflow after `acc * 10 + d` has already overflowed.

fw-cmd-parser.prompt: Split a command line in place on spaces and tabs into an argv array: `parse_tokens(line, argv, max_args)`.
ideas: Loop: skip whitespace, record the token start, scan to the next whitespace, write a NUL, repeat.
Stop once `count == max_args`; never write `argv[max_args]`.
fw-cmd-parser.bug: Stepping past the string's terminator when the last token ends there.

fw-hex-codec.prompt: `hex_to_bytes` and `bytes_to_hex`, with bounds checks and bad-digit rejection.
ideas: Nibble value: three ranges, '0'–'9', 'a'–'f', 'A'–'F'; anything else fails.
Validate the length (even, fits `out_cap`) before writing.
Encode with `"0123456789abcdef"[b >> 4]` and `[b & 0xF]`.
fw-hex-codec.bug: Forgetting room for the NUL (`2n + 1`), or a loose range check that accepts ':' or 'g'.

fw-ring-buffer.prompt: Byte ring buffer over caller storage with a `full` flag: push, pop, available, free space.
ideas: `head == tail` means empty or full; the flag decides. Set it when a push makes the indices meet, clear it on every pop.
Advance an index with `(i + 1) % capacity`.
Available = `full ? capacity : (write - read + capacity) % capacity`.
fw-ring-buffer.bug: Never clearing `full` on pop, so the buffer reports full forever.

fw-adc-moving-avg.prompt: Moving average of the last 10 eight-bit ADC samples, O(1) per sample.
ideas: Running sum: subtract the sample being overwritten, add the new one, advance the slot.
The window starts as ten zeros, so always divide by 10.
fw-adc-moving-avg.bug: Re-summing all 10 samples every call, or a running sum in `uint8_t`.

fw-lower-bracket.prompt: Largest `i` with `xs[i] <= target` in a sorted `int32_t` array, by binary search.
ideas: Search `[lo, hi)` for the first element greater than target; the answer is that index minus 1.
Compute `mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2`; target below `xs[0]` returns false.
fw-lower-bracket.bug: An infinite loop from `lo = mid`, or `size_t` underflow when computing `i - 1`.

fw-subarray-sum.prompt: Find a contiguous run of non-negative values summing exactly to target; return `[start, end)`.
ideas: Two pointers: extend `end` while sum < target, advance `start` while sum > target.
This only works because the values are non-negative, so the window sum only grows as it extends.
target 0 is the empty window `[0, 0)`.
fw-subarray-sum.bug: Letting `start` pass `end`, or a 32-bit running sum that overflows.

fw-longest-unique-c.prompt: Length of the longest substring with no repeated byte, without malloc.
ideas: Sliding window `[lo, hi)` plus `last[256]` holding each byte's last index + 1 (0 = unseen).
On a repeat inside the window (`last[c] > lo`), jump `lo = last[c]`; `lo` never moves back.
Index with `(unsigned char)s[hi]`.
fw-longest-unique-c.bug: Moving `lo` backward on a repeat outside the window ('abba'), or indexing with a negative `char`.

valid-parentheses.prompt: In C: is a string of `()[]{}` balanced and properly nested?
ideas: Push openers onto a char stack; a closer must match the top, which you pop.
Valid only if the stack is empty at the end.
valid-parentheses.bug: Popping an empty stack on a leading closer, or returning true with openers left over.

fw-intrusive-list.prompt: push_front, pop_front, remove and count on an intrusive singly linked list via `node_t **head`.
ideas: Remove with a pointer-to-pointer walk: `for (node_t **pp = head; *pp; pp = &(*pp)->next) if (*pp == node) { *pp = node->next; return true; }`.
pop_front on an empty list returns NULL.
fw-intrusive-list.bug: Special-casing the head and forgetting to update `*head` when removing the first node.

fw-list-reverse.prompt: Reverse a singly linked list in place and return the new head.
ideas: `prev = NULL; while (cur) { next = cur->next; cur->next = prev; prev = cur; cur = next; } return prev;`
fw-list-reverse.bug: Overwriting `cur->next` before saving it, which loses the rest of the list.

fw-crc16.prompt: CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE: poly 0x1021, init 0xFFFF, no reflection, no final XOR; `"123456789"` gives 0x29B1.
ideas: Per byte: `crc ^= (uint16_t)byte << 8`, then 8 times: `crc = (crc & 0x8000) ? (crc << 1) ^ 0x1021 : crc << 1`.
Keep `crc` a `uint16_t` (or mask with 0xFFFF) after each shift.
Empty input returns the init value.
fw-crc16.bug: XOR-ing the byte into the low byte, which is the reflected variant.

fw-endian-serial.prompt: Encode and decode a fixed sensor message as little-endian bytes, field by field.
ideas: Write `out[i] = (uint8_t)(v >> (8 * k))`; read `v |= (uint32_t)in[i] << (8 * k)`.
Signed field: encode `(uint16_t)temp`; decode into a `uint16_t`, then cast to `int16_t`.
Check the buffer length before touching it.
fw-endian-serial.bug: `in[3] << 24` on a promoted `int` (sets the sign bit), or memcpy of the struct (padding and host byte order).

fw-packet-parser.prompt: Byte-at-a-time parser for `0xAA | LEN | PAYLOAD | CHECKSUM`: packet, error, or need more.
ideas: One switch on the state: WAIT_START, READ_LEN, READ_PAYLOAD, READ_CKSUM.
Checksum = low 8 bits of LEN + the payload bytes; accumulate as bytes arrive.
An oversized LEN or bad checksum returns an error and goes back to hunting for 0xAA.
fw-packet-parser.bug: Not resetting the payload index and running checksum on resync.

fw-gpio-debounce.prompt: Debounce a GPIO with timestamps: commit a new level only after it holds for `debounce_ms`.
ideas: Track a pending level and its start time; commit when `(uint32_t)(now - start) >= debounce_ms`.
A bounce back to the committed level cancels the pending change.
Report the event once, on the update that commits.
fw-gpio-debounce.bug: `now >= start + debounce_ms`, which breaks when the counter wraps.

fw-mipi-raw10.prompt: Unpack MIPI RAW10 (4 pixels in 5 bytes) into 16-bit pixels.
ideas: Bytes 0–3 are each pixel's top 8 bits; byte 4 holds the four 2-bit LSB pairs, pixel 0 in bits 1:0.
`px[i] = (b[i] << 2) | ((b[4] >> (2 * i)) & 3)`, then advance 5 bytes in and 4 pixels out.
fw-mipi-raw10.bug: Taking pixel 0's LSBs from bits 7:6 of byte 4.

fw-can-signal.prompt: Read, sign-extend and write an N-bit signal at any bit offset in an 8-byte Intel-order CAN frame.
ideas: Assemble the frame into a `uint64_t` (byte 0 lowest), then shift and mask.
Build masks in 64 bits, `(1ULL << len) - 1`, so `len == 32` is defined.
Sign-extend: if bit `len - 1` is set, subtract `1LL << len`.
Write: `raw = (raw & ~mask) | (((uint64_t)value << start) & mask)`.
fw-can-signal.bug: `(1u << len) - 1` with `len == 32` (undefined), or setting bits without clearing the old ones.

fw-q16-mul.prompt: Q16.16 multiply and int conversions that stay exact when `a * b` overflows 32 bits.
ideas: `(q16_t)(((int64_t)a * b) >> 16)`: widen before you multiply.
from_int is `x << 16` (multiply by 65536 for negatives, avoiding UB); to_int is `x >> 16`.
Right shift of a negative value is implementation-defined; it is arithmetic on every real target.
fw-q16-mul.bug: Multiplying in 32 bits and widening afterward, when the product has already overflowed.

fw-q15-sat.prompt: Q15 saturating add/sub, and multiply with round-to-nearest; -1 × -1 must give 0x7FFF.
ideas: Widen to `int32_t`, compute, then clamp to [INT16_MIN, INT16_MAX].
mul: `(a * b + (1 << 14)) >> 15` rounds half up; only -32768 × -32768 then needs the clamp.
No float; no signed overflow.
fw-q15-sat.bug: Skipping the multiply's clamp, so -1 × -1 wraps to -1.

fw-ema-filter.prompt: Integer EMA with alpha = 1/2^k that settles exactly on a constant input.
ideas: Keep the state scaled by 2^k: `state += x - (state >> k)`, output `state >> k`.
The unscaled `y += (x - y) >> k` stalls up to 2^k - 1 short of the target.
Initialize the state to `initial` scaled by 2^k (multiply, so negatives aren't UB).
fw-ema-filter.bug: The unscaled update, which never reaches the input.

fw-interp-table.prompt: Piecewise-linear interpolation over a sorted calibration table; false outside the range.
ideas: Find the segment with `x0 <= x <= x1` (a scan or binary search).
`y0 + (int32_t)((int64_t)(y1 - y0) * (x - x0) / (x1 - x0))`: widen the product.
Multiply before you divide.
fw-interp-table.bug: A 32-bit product that overflows, or dividing first and losing precision.

fw-median-filter.prompt: Median of the last n samples (n odd, at most 15), updated each sample, lower middle while warming up.
ideas: Keep arrival order in the ring; copy the live samples to a scratch array and sort the copy (insertion sort; n ≤ 15).
Median of k sorted values is index `(k - 1) / 2`, the lower middle when k is even.
Use `count` until the window fills.
fw-median-filter.bug: Sorting the ring in place, which destroys arrival order so the wrong sample leaves the window.

fw-mmio-rw.prompt: 32-bit MMIO read and write with range and alignment checks against a fake register window.
ideas: Valid when `addr >= BASE`, `addr - BASE <= SIZE - 4` and `(addr & 3) == 0`.
Subtract before comparing so nothing can overflow near UINTPTR_MAX.
Store little-endian, byte by byte.
fw-mmio-rw.bug: `addr + 4 <= BASE + SIZE`, which wraps for huge addresses, or accepting the last 1–3 bytes of the window.

fw-spi-driver.prompt: SPI byte transfer against a register struct: poll TX ready, write, poll RX ready, check error, read.
ideas: Each poll loop re-reads the status register and decrements a timeout, returning SPI_TIMEOUT at 0.
Check the error bit only after RX ready is seen.
Init always sets the enable bit, whatever the flags.
fw-spi-driver.bug: Spinning on a status value read once, instead of re-reading the register every iteration.

fw-aligned-malloc.prompt: `aligned_malloc(size, align)` and `aligned_free(ptr)` using only malloc and free.
ideas: Allocate `size + align - 1 + sizeof(void *)`, then round up past room for one pointer.
Store the raw pointer just below the aligned block: `((void **)aligned)[-1] = raw`.
Round up as `(addr + align - 1) & ~(uintptr_t)(align - 1)` on a `uintptr_t`.
fw-aligned-malloc.bug: Freeing the aligned pointer instead of the stored raw one.

fw-bump-alloc.prompt: Aligned bump allocator over a fixed buffer: alloc with any power-of-two alignment, reset only.
ideas: Align up: `(x + a - 1) & ~(a - 1)`.
Check that the aligned offset plus `sz` fits before committing; on failure return NULL and leave the offset alone.
fw-bump-alloc.bug: Checking for space before adding the alignment padding.

fw-pool-alloc.prompt: Fixed-block pool over caller storage, with O(1) alloc and free using a free list kept inside the free blocks.
ideas: Init threads every block onto the list: `*(void **)block = next_block`.
Alloc pops: `p = head; head = *(void **)p`. Free pushes: `*(void **)p = head; head = p`.
Reject block sizes smaller than `sizeof(void *)`.
fw-pool-alloc.bug: Accepting a pointer in free without checking it lies inside storage on a block boundary.

fw-uart-rx.prompt: Lock-free UART RX buffer: the ISR writes `head` and `dropped`, the main loop writes `tail`.
ideas: Free-running counters: used = `head - tail` (unsigned wrap is fine); full when used == capacity.
ISR: store the byte, then advance head. Reader: copy bytes out, then advance tail.
Each side writes only its own index; read the other side's index once into a local.
fw-uart-rx.bug: Advancing `head` before storing the byte, so the reader can see a slot that isn't written yet.

fw-uart-word-stream.prompt: Print UART bytes from an ISR one word per line from the main loop, losing nothing.
ideas: The ISR only copies `UART_RX_REGISTER` into a ring buffer; all printing happens in `main_loop`.
main_loop drains what has arrived, printing a newline for each space.
Shared indices are `volatile`, and each side writes only its own.
fw-uart-word-stream.bug: Printing from the ISR, or a consumer that also writes the producer's index.

fw-timer-sched.prompt: Software timers on a wrapping 32-bit ms counter: start, cancel, poll, one-shot and periodic.
ideas: Due check: `(uint32_t)(now - deadline) < 0x80000000u`, i.e. `(int32_t)(now - deadline) >= 0`.
Periodic: `deadline += period`, not `now + period`, so it never drifts.
Use the lowest free slot; cancel rejects out-of-range and inactive ids.
fw-timer-sched.bug: `now >= deadline`, which fires everything immediately (or never) across the wrap.

fw-find-bit-pattern.prompt: Find the first bit offset of 0xFE6B2840 in an MSB-first byte stream; the match may be unaligned.
ideas: Shift bits into a `uint32_t` window one at a time: `w = (w << 1) | bit`.
Compare only once 32 bits are in; the match starts at bits consumed minus 32.
Handle NULL or fewer than 4 bytes, and never read past the end.
fw-find-bit-pattern.bug: Comparing before the window holds 32 real bits, or returning the end offset instead of the start.

fw-hash-table.prompt: Fixed-capacity `uint32_t` → `uint32_t` map with put, get and delete, no heap; every key is valid.
ideas: Open addressing with linear probing; a state per slot: EMPTY, USED, DELETED.
Delete leaves a tombstone so keys further along the chain stay reachable.
Put searches the whole chain for the key first, then inserts into the first tombstone or empty slot.
Bound every probe loop at HT_CAP steps.
fw-hash-table.bug: Delete marking the slot EMPTY, which breaks lookups for keys further down the chain.

fw-bitmap-alloc.prompt: Allocate the lowest free ID, or the lowest run of n free IDs, from a 128-bit bitmap, and free IDs.
ideas: Skip full words (`== 0xFFFFFFFF`); `~w & (w + 1)` isolates the lowest zero bit (or use `__builtin_ctz(~w)`).
Runs: count consecutive zero bits across word boundaries, and mark nothing until the whole run is found.
Use `1u << b`, never `1 << 31`.
fw-bitmap-alloc.bug: Marking bits during the search, then failing with the map half changed.

fw-mini-printf.prompt: `mini_snprintf` with %d %u %x %c %s %%, a 0 flag and width, truncation and the C99 return value.
ideas: Route every character through one `put(c)` that writes only while `len + 1 < cap` but always counts.
Numbers: take the magnitude as unsigned (`0u - (unsigned)v` covers INT_MIN), emit digits reversed from a temp buffer.
Pad with spaces before the sign, zeros after it.
Terminate at `min(len, cap - 1)` when cap > 0; return the full length.
fw-mini-printf.bug: Returning the truncated length instead of the length the full output would have.

fw-heap-alloc.prompt: First-fit malloc and free over a caller's arena, with splitting and merging of free neighbours.
ideas: Every block starts with a header (size + free flag); blocks tile the arena, so the next header is at `hdr + size`.
Alloc: round n up to 8, walk blocks first fit, split when the remainder can hold a header plus 8 bytes.
Free: mark free, merge with the next block if free, and with the previous one (walk from the start, or keep a footer).
fw-heap-alloc.bug: Merging only forward, so freeing in reverse order never rebuilds the big block.
